html:
In 802 Jayavarman II was consecrated as universal monarch on the sacred mountain of Phnom Kulen, north of Angkor. Khmer tradition treats this as the founding of the Khmer Empire.

Jayavarman II had spent years uniting the rival Khmer states left by Chenla. The ceremony, known from a later inscription, declared Cambodia free from Java and set up the cult of the god-king linked to Shiva.

His successors moved the capital to the Angkor plain, where they built reservoirs such as the West Baray and temples culminating in Angkor Wat. Recent laser surveys have found a large city on Phnom Kulen from his time. See Sambor Prei Kuk.
